turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Yeah, um... well, I came in because I'm just having a really hard time lately. I drive a cab, and even when I know for a fact I did my safety check on the car, this thought just keeps hitting me that I missed something. Like, I keep thinking somebody could get hurt because of me, or my boss is gonna say I lied about checking it. And I just... I can't make the thought shut up. It doesn't matter if I'm driving or just trying to sit down and study, it just won't stop.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient reports recurrent, intrusive, and persistent doubts about missing vehicle safety checks and causing harm that they cannot suppress or stop despite knowing they completed the check.

turns.doctor_question: When that thought hits that you might have missed something on the car, do you go back and check it again?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. Um... before I can even take a ride, I keep going around the car checking everything. The tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, my paperwork... I just check them over and over again. Sometimes I even take pictures of everything just to prove to myself I did it. And if the routine doesn't feel exactly right, I have to restart the whole check from the very beginning. It gets so bad that I'm doing it even when passengers are literally standing there waiting for me and I'm already late. I just have to be sure.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive checking rituals and restarting the routine from the beginning if it does not feel right, causing functional impairment even when passengers are waiting.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel that the amount of checking you do is excessive, even though you still feel driven to do it?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, for sure. I mean... I know it's way over the top. Logically, I know the car is fine after the first time I look at it. It's definitely excessive. But... even knowing that doesn't help at all. I still have to do it. Like, I know I probably look crazy making people wait while I stare at a tire I just checked two minutes ago, but the feeling that I missed something is just so strong I can't ignore it.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes feeling driven to perform repetitive and excessive checking behaviors (e.g., repeatedly checking a car tire) despite logically knowing it is unnecessary.

turns.doctor_question: About how much time in a typical day do these checking routines take up?
turns.patient_response: I don't really know exactly how much time it takes up. I mean, I've never actually timed it or anything. It's just... it feels like it takes up a lot of my day, honestly. Especially before I start a shift, but I couldn't give you an exact number of hours or minutes.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient confirms having checking routines that take up a significant portion of their day, especially before work shifts, indicative of checking compulsions.

turns.doctor_question: Have these checking rituals caused serious problems in your work, studies, or daily life?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, they really have. Um... at work, I've actually lost rides and gotten warnings because I just can't get on the road on time. And I'm trying to study for my CDL, but that keeps getting pushed back because so much of my day just gets eaten up by all this. 

It affects my personal life, too. I barely see my friends anymore. I'm always either behind on my shifts or trying to catch up after all the delays from checking everything. So, yeah, it's causing a lot of problems.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient confirms engaging in extensive checking rituals that consume significant parts of their day and cause major functional delays.

turns.doctor_question: When these thoughts about the car come up, do they feel intrusive and unwanted—like they pop into your mind even when you don’t want them there?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, exactly. That's actually why I came in. Like, I'll do my safety check on the cab, and I know I did it. But then this thought just hits me out of nowhere that I missed something. It just pops into my head that a tire is going to blow or the brakes will fail, and somebody's going to get hurt, or my boss is going to think I lied about doing the check. I definitely don't want those thoughts, but I just can't make them shut up. It happens all the time while I'm driving, or even when I'm just sitting there trying to study for my CDL.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient explicitly confirms having intrusive, unwanted thoughts about vehicle failure and potential harm that pop into their head despite safety checks and that they cannot suppress.

turns.doctor_question: Do you recognize that these thoughts and checking behaviors are coming from your own mind, even though they feel unreasonable?
turns.patient_response:
I'm not really sure. Um... I mean, I guess I know nobody else is putting the thoughts in my head, but... they don't really feel unreasonable to me. Not when it's happening, anyway. 

It feels like a real warning, like something terrible is actually about to happen with the cab if I don't go back and check. So, I don't know. It's hard for me to just say it's all in my own mind when it feels that real.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from the cab safety issue, do you spend a lot of time worrying about other parts of your life?
turns.patient_response:
Um... no, not really. It's pretty much just the cab. I mean, I guess I think about normal stuff, like passing my CDL test or paying my bills, but it's not like a constant worry or anything. 

The safety checks are what really take up all my time and energy. I don't really stress about other parts of my life the way I do about that.
